correctness.rationale: A backward graphical ancestor represents affine RAP position as conditional expectation of its lattice ancestor. The total ancestor jump count has Poisson law with mean mu(p+q)s, bounding every fixed moment polynomially in s. Truncating ancestry to radius R creates independent disjoint-label environments; escape probability is bounded by an R-step Poisson tail, and Jensen yields L^m convergence. Thus fixed-age widely separated tracers factor jointly. A common reset clock has age min(Exp(r),t) and independent postreset motion; exponential moments justify mixing, then all distinct-index subset product moments converge to (vA)^|B|. The joint moment-cumulant partition identity gives v^n kappa_n(A), and stationary Exp cumulants are (n-1)!(v/r)^n. Independent symbolic expansion verified exact finite-time second and third cumulants, including prior Eq42. Limits are fixed n and diverging separation only.

value.rationale: A natural higher-order observable of a precisely established single-file model displays a universal infinite family of nondecaying correlations despite fixed-age local mixing. It is a meaningful structural extension from two-point to n-point joint behavior, not a trivial reformatting of a known covariance; it does not claim to solve single-tracer high moments.

final_claim: For any fixed n distinct RAP tracers with pairwise label separations tending to infinity under a common global Poisson reset, conditional on common reset age their joint law factors; stationary connected one-insertion cumulants equal (n-1)!(h mu (p-q)/r)^n.
limitations: An unindexed general interacting-particle graphical mixing theorem may already imply the conditional-product limit.
